children: 一千年前，欧洲并不存在。在公元千年到来之前十年，生活在欧亚大陆西端的大约三千万人，并没有充分理由把自己看作一个由历史与共同命运连接起来的单一人群。他们也确实没有这样看。诚然，罗马帝国的解体使今天我们所称的欧洲的相当一部分地区依然由道路、贸易、宗教和集体记忆连接在一起。但那个曾经的罗马世界遗漏了莱茵河以东和黑海以北的很大一片地区。晚期帝国也并非专属于欧洲；它曾环绕整个地中海，伸入亚洲和非洲。

A thousand years ago, Europe did not exist. A decade before the Millennium, the roughly thirty million people who lived at the western end of the Eurasian land mass had no compelling reason to think of themselves as a single set of people, connected by history and common fate. Nor did they. The disintegration of the Roman Empire, it is true, had left a significant part of what we now call Europe connected by roads, trade, religion, and collective memory. But that once-Roman world omitted much of the area east of the Rhine and north of the Black Sea. Nor was the late empire exclusively European; it had extended all around the Mediterranean into Asia and Africa.

从贸易与文化接触的角度看，公元千年时的“欧洲”分成了三四个松散相连的集群：一个东部地带，大体相当于今天的欧洲俄罗斯，它同拜占庭以及横贯亚洲的主要商路保持着牢固联系；一个由穆斯林、基督徒和犹太人共享的地中海世界，它同中东和亚洲各大都市的联系甚至更为紧密；一个后罗马时代的城市、市镇、道路与河流体系，其密度在从意大利中部到佛兰德的一道弧带上最高，并向德意志和法兰西辐射；或许还有一个独特的北方集群，包括斯堪的纳维亚和不列颠群岛。（当然，这些标签大多犯了时代错置的错误；除非采用一整套笨重的地理命名惯例，我们别无选择，只能使用“德意志”“不列颠群岛”这类名称，同时大声提醒：它们并不意味着政治或文化上的连通。）

From the viewpoint of trade and cultural contact, Millennial "Europe" broke into three or four loosely connected clusters: an eastern band corresponding roughly to today's European Russia, which maintained strong connections to Byzantium and to the major trade routes across Asia; a Mediterranean shared by Muslims, Christians, and Jews that was even more strongly linked to the great metropolises of the Middle East and Asia; a post-Roman system of cities, towns, roads, and rivers that was densest in an arc from central Italy to Flanders, but radiated into Germany and France; perhaps a distinct northern cluster including Scandinavia and the British Isles. (Many of these labels, to be sure, commit the crime of anachronism; short of adopting a ponderous set of geographic conventions, we have no alternative to using such designations as "Germany" and "British Isles" with a loud warning that they do not imply political or cultural connectedness.)

公元990年，穆斯林的领地控制了罗马帝国旧疆域的很大一部分：地中海的全部南岸和伊比利亚半岛的大部分，更不用说众多地中海岛屿及其北岸的若干据点。一个联系松散的拜占庭帝国从意大利东部延伸到黑海东端，而在它以北，一个更为模糊的俄罗斯国家一直伸展到波罗的海。一个丹麦王国把权力从波罗的海西部一直投送到不列颠群岛，而变动不居的波兰、波希米亚和匈牙利诸公国则控制着波罗的海以南的地区。在它们以西，是一个自称继承查理曼遗产的萨克森帝国；再往同一方向，是于格·卡佩统治的法兰西王国。

In the year 990 Muslim dominions controlled a major share of the Roman Empire's former space: all of the Mediterranean's southern shores and most of the Iberian peninsula, not to mention numerous Mediterranean islands and a few points along its northern coast. A loosely linked Byzantine empire extended from eastern Italy to the Black Sea's eastern end, while to its north an even more indefinite Russian state stretched to the Baltic. A Danish kingdom wielded power from the western Baltic over to the British Isles, while shifting Polish, Bohemian, and Hungarian principalities controlled the territory south of the Baltic. To their west lay a Saxon empire, claimant to the heritage of Charlemagne, while still farther in the same direction Hugh Capet ruled the kingdom of France.

children: 然而，这些似曾相识的地名不应掩盖当时遍布于日后欧洲全境的主权的极度碎裂。公元990年的皇帝、国王、诸侯、公爵、哈里发、苏丹以及其他权贵，是以征服者、贡赋收取者和食利者的身份立足的，而不是作为持久而细密地规制其领地内生活的国家元首。而且，在他们的管辖范围内，对手和表面上的下属常常为自己的利益动用武力，而很少顾及他们名义上的君主的利益。私人军队在欧洲大陆的大部分地区大量涌现。欧洲任何地方都不存在类似中央集权的民族国家
的东西。

None of these half-familiar place names, however, should disguise the enormous fragmentation of sovereignty then prevailing throughout the territory that would become Europe. The emperors, kings, princes, dukes, caliphs, sultans, and other potentates of AD 990 prevailed as conquerors, tribute-takers, and rentiers, not as heads of state that durably and densely regulated life within their realms. Inside their jurisdictions, furthermore, rivals and ostensible subordinates commonly used armed force on behalf of their own interests while paying little attention to the interests of their nominal sovereigns. Private armies proliferated through much of the continent. Nothing like a centralized national state existed anywhere in Europe.

children: 在这些蔓延而短命的诸国所围成的圈内，主权碎裂得更厉害：数以百计的公国、主教区、城邦和其他权力机构，在各自都城周边的狭小腹地中行使彼此重叠的控制。公元千年之际，教宗、拜占庭皇帝和神圣罗马帝国皇帝都声称拥有意大利半岛的大部分，但实际上几乎每一座重要城市及其腹地都作为一个政治上的自由行动者行事。（公元1200年，仅意大利半岛就拥有两三百个各自独立的城邦：Waley 1969: 11。）除了穆斯林地区城市化程度较高这一例外，国家规模与城市密度之间的相关性是负的：城市繁盛之处，主权便崩解。

Within the ring formed by these sprawling, ephemeral states sovereignty fragmented even more, as hundreds of principalities, bishoprics, city-states, and other authorities exercised overlapping control in the small hinterlands of their capitals. At the Millennium the pope, the Byzantine emperor and the Holy Roman emperor claimed most of the Italian peninsula, but in fact almost every important city and its hinterland operated as a political free agent. (In AD 1200, the Italian peninsula alone hosted two or three hundred distinct city-states: Waley 1969: 11.) Except for the relative urbanization of Muslim lands, the correlation between size of states and density of cities was negative: where cities swarmed, sovereignty crumbled.

再过不久，过去一千年间城市与国家变迁的粗略年表就会开始各就各位。不过在此之前，我们不妨先以500年为间隔作一个任意的比较，好对变化之大有个感觉。到1490年，地图和现实都已大为改观。武装的基督徒正把穆斯林统治者逐出他们在欧洲大陆西半部的最后一块主要领地——格拉纳达。一个伊斯兰的奥斯曼帝国已在亚得里亚海与波斯之间取代了基督教的拜占庭人。奥斯曼人正在东地中海一点点消磨威尼斯的势力，并向巴尔干推进。（他们与被威胁的格拉纳达结盟，也开始在西地中海进行最初的冒险。）此外，在经历了许多个世纪、欧洲战争始终局限于地区范围、只有偶尔的十字军才使阿尔卑斯山以北的国家在军事上卷入地中海之后，法国和西班牙的国王正开始争夺意大利的霸权。

Soon a rough chronology of changes in cities and states over the last thousand years will start to fall into place. In the meantime, however, let us settle for an arbitrary comparison at 500-year intervals, just to get a sense of how much changed. By 1490, the map and the reality had altered greatly. Armed Christians were driving Muslim rulers from their last major territory on the continent's western half - Granada. An Islamic Ottoman empire had displaced the Christian Byzantines between the Adriatic and Persia. The Ottomans were grinding away at Venetian power in the eastern Mediterranean and advancing into the Balkans. (In alliance with threatened Granada, they were also pursuing their first adventures in the western Mediterranean.) After centuries during which European wars had remained regional, and only an occasional crusade had involved the transalpine states militarily in the Mediterranean, furthermore, the kings of France and Spain were beginning to struggle for hegemony in Italy.
1490年，在欧洲的周边屹立着一些统治大片领土的君主：不仅有奥斯曼帝国，还有匈牙利、波兰、立陶宛、莫斯科公国、条顿骑士团的领地、斯堪的纳维亚联盟、英格兰、法兰西、西班牙、葡萄牙、那不勒斯。这些强权主要靠地租和贡赋为生，并通过在自己地盘内享有高度自主性的地方权贵进行统治；这些权贵常常抵制甚至拒不承认王权。然而，1490年的大国王和大公们总体上正在巩固并扩大自己的领地。

Around Europe's periphery, in 1490, stood rulers who dominated substantial territories: not only the Ottoman Empire, but also Hungary, Poland, Lithuania, Muscovy, the lands of the Teutonic Order, the Scandinavian Union, England, France, Spain, Portugal, Naples. Those powers lived largely from rents and tributes, and ruled through regional magnates who enjoyed great autonomy within their own terrains; the magnates frequently resisted or even rejected royal power. Yet the great kings and dukes of 1490 were, on the whole, consolidating and extending their domains.

于是，在较大国家组成的残缺圆环内部，欧洲仍是一片主权高度碎裂的土地。诚然，一个散布各处的哈布斯堡帝国正开始横贯大陆，而威尼斯控制着亚得里亚海的一段重要弧线。但从意大利北部到佛兰德、向东直到匈牙利和波兰那不确定的边界，这一地带分裂为数百个形式上独立的公国、公爵领、主教区、城邦和其他政治实体，它们一般只能在自己的都城近旁腹地使用武力；仅南德意志一地，除众多主教区、公爵领和公国外，就有69个自由市（Brady 1985: 10）。J. R. 黑尔沉思道：“尽管制图师可以在15世纪中叶舆论认为属于神圣罗马帝国的地区周围画出一条边界——即法兰西与匈牙利之间、丹麦与意大利北部之间那片以日耳曼人为主的地区——他却无法把那众多自认为实际独立或可能独立的城市、诸侯飞地和好战的教会领地涂上颜色，而不让读者觉得他患上了视网膜疾病”（Hale 1985: 14）。欧洲的8000万人口分属大约200个国家、准国家、小国和类似国家的组织。

Inside the broken circle of larger states, then, Europe remained a land of intensely fragmented sovereignty. A scattered Habsburg empire, it is true, was beginning to reach across the continent, while Venice dominated an important arc of the Adriatic. But the zone from northern Italy to Flanders, and east to the uncertain borders of Hungary and Poland, broke into hundreds of formally independent principalities, duchies, bishoprics, city-states, and other political entities that generally could use force only in the immediate hinterlands of their capitals; south Germany alone included 69 free cities in addition to its multiple bishoprics, duchies, and principalities (Brady 1985: 10). "In spite of the border which a cartographer can draw around the area which opinion in the midfifteenth century accepted as within the Holy Roman Empire, that is the chiefly Germanic zone between France and Hungary, and Denmark and northern Italy," muses J. R. Hale, "he cannot colour in the multitude of cities, princely enclaves and militant ecclesiastical territories that saw themselves as actually or potentially independent, without giving the reader an impression that he is suffering from a disease of the retina" (Hale 1985: 14). Europe's 80 million people divided into something like 200 states, would-be states, statelets, and statelike organizations.

children: 又过了五个世纪，到1990年，欧洲人已大大推进了整合工作。如今有六亿人生活在这块大陆的疆界之内。大陆上已不再有穆斯林国家，尽管一个强大的伊斯兰世界在欧洲以南和东南方充满争斗地繁荣着，而且西班牙、巴尔干和土耳其仍存留着引人注目的穆斯林文化遗迹。一个庞大的俄罗斯国家在东部成形，一直延伸到北极和太平洋，而一个幅员辽阔的土耳其则向东南跨过了亚洲边界。大陆的大部分地区已归并为面积至少40,000平方英里的国家，不包括殖民地和属地：保加利亚、捷克斯洛伐克、芬兰、法兰西、两个德意志国家、希腊、意大利、挪威、波兰、罗马尼亚、西班牙、瑞典、土耳其、联合王国，以及尚未解体的苏联。卢森堡和安道尔之类的微型国家虽然比1490年存在的许多政治实体还大，却已成为奇观。按照不同的计数规则，整个欧洲只划分为25至28个国家。

By 1990, another five centuries later, Europeans had greatly extended the work of consolidation. Six hundred million people now lived within the continent's perimeter. No Muslim state remained on the continent, although a powerful Islamic world thrived contentiously to the south and southeast of Europe and impressive residues of Muslim culture survived in Spain, the Balkans, and Turkey. A giant Russian state had taken shape on the east and stretched all the way to the Arctic and the Pacific, while a spacious Turkey crossed the Asian border to the southeast. Much of the continent had settled into states that occupied at least 40,000 square miles, not including colonies and dependencies: Bulgaria, Czechoslovakia, Finland, France, each of the two Germanies, Greece, Italy, Norway, Poland, Romania, Spain, Sweden, Turkey, the United Kingdom, and the not yet splintered USSR. Microstates such as Luxembourg and Andorra, although larger than many of the political entities that existed in 1490, had become curiosities. Depending on the rules for counting, the whole of Europe divided into a mere 25 to 28 states.

民族国家——即相对集权、分化且自主，并成功主张在大片连续而边界清晰的领土内优先使用暴力的组织——用了很长时间才主导欧洲地图。在990年，庄园、地方领主、军事劫掠者、设防村庄、贸易城镇、城邦和修道院的世界中，没有任何东西预示会整合为民族国家。1490年，未来仍是开放的；尽管“王国”一词被频繁使用，各种类型的帝国仍占据着欧洲版图的大部分，而联邦式的政治联合体在大陆某些地区依然可行。1490年之后的某个时候，欧洲人封闭了那些替代性的机会，果断地走上了创建一个几乎完全由相对自主的民族国家构成的体系之路。

It took a long time for national states - relatively centralized, differentiated, and autonomous organizations successfully claiming priority in the use of force within large, contiguous, and clearly bounded territories - to dominate the European map. In 990 nothing about the world of manors, local lords, military raiders, fortified villages, trading towns, city-states, and monasteries foretold a consolidation into national states. In 1490 the future remained open; despite the frequent use of the word "kingdom," empires of one sort or another claimed most of the European landscape, and federations remained viable in some parts of the continent. Some time after 1490 Europeans foreclosed those alternative opportunities, and set off decisively toward the creation of a system consisting almost entirely of relatively autonomous national states.

另一方面，国家的数目减少了，面积扩大了。为了绘制这一变动中的地图，我们必须宽泛地使用“国家”一词，把任何掌握大量强制手段、并成功主张在至少一块边界清晰的领土内对所有其他强制手段使用者享有持久优先权的组织都包括进来。公元990年，相对较大的穆斯林国家控制着西地中海的大部分，包括西班牙南部和非洲北岸。其他规模可观的国家包括法兰西王国、萨克森帝国、丹麦王国、基辅罗斯、波兰、匈牙利、波希米亚和拜占庭帝国。总体而言，这些政治实体的统治者从名义上受其控制的领土上收取贡赋。但在其家乡地区之外，他们几乎无法管理自己声称拥有的领地，其权威不断受到敌对权贵的挑战，其中也包括那些名义上属于他们的代理人和封臣。

States, on the other hand, diminished in number and increased in area. In order to draw the changing map, we must apply the term "state" generously, to include any organization that commanded substantial means of coercion and successfully claimed durable priority over all other users of coercion within at least one clearly bounded territory. In the year 990 relatively large Muslim states dominated much of the western Mediterranean, including southern Spain and Africa's north coast. Other sizeable states included the kingdom of France, the Saxon empire, the Danish kingdom, Kievan Russia, Poland, Hungary, Bohemia, and the Byzantine Empire. On the whole, the rulers of these political entities drew tribute from the territories nominally under their control. But outside their home regions they barely administered their supposed domains, and saw their authority continually contested by rival potentates, including their own putative agents and vassals.

以匈牙利为例。这个国家起源于马扎尔人的征服，而马扎尔人是众多从欧亚草原入侵欧洲的武装游牧民族之一。10世纪时，大部分马扎尔人从伏尔加河一带迁来，压倒了居住在喀尔巴阡盆地（即我们今天所称的匈牙利）中人数较少的农耕与林居斯拉夫人（Pamlenyi 1975: 21-5）。一旦他们迁到喀尔巴阡山脉以西，天然牧场的短缺就迫使任何掠夺性的游牧民要么撤退，要么削减人数，要么下马定居（Lindner 1981）。经过一个世纪的劫掠，此时已基督教化的匈牙利人日益定居于农业，生活在一块几乎见不到城市的领土上。

Consider Hungary, a state that grew from conquest by Magyars, one of many armed nomadic peoples who invaded Europe from the Eurasian steppe. During the tenth century, the bulk of the Magyars migrated from the Volga and overwhelmed the smaller number of tilling and forest-dwelling Slavs who inhabited the Carpathian Basin, which we now call Hungary (Pamlenyi 1975: 21-5). Once they moved west of the Carpathians, the shortage of natural pasture forced any predatory nomads to withdraw, thin their numbers, or dismount (Lindner 1981). After a century of marauding, the now-Christianized Hungarians settled increasingly into agriculture inside a territory almost without cities.
他们的农业基础并未阻止匈牙利贵族与邻邦交战、争夺王位继承权，或参与欧洲的联姻与结盟游戏。此外，他们对武装力量的控制使他们能够把奴隶和自由人一并驱向共同的农奴地位。随着封建农业的繁荣，市镇成长起来，矿山把金属输往欧洲其他地区，该地区的商路也与中欧和西欧的商路交织在一起。德意志资本逐渐支配了匈牙利的商业和工业。然而，匈牙利的市镇始终紧紧从属于它们的贵族领主，直到15世纪王权开始对它们施加控制。

Their agricultural base did not prevent the Hungarian nobility from warring with their neighbors, struggling over the royal succession, or playing the European game of marriages and alliances. Their control of armed force, furthermore, permitted them to drive slaves and freemen alike toward a common serfdom. Towns grew up as feudal agriculture prospered, mines exported metals to the rest of Europe, and the region's trade routes knitted together with those of central and western Europe. German capital came to dominate Hungarian commerce and industry. Hungary's towns, however, remained tightly subordinate to their noble lords until, during the fifteenth century, the crown began to exert control over them.

15世纪后期，亚诺什·匈雅提国王和他的儿子马蒂亚斯·科尔维努斯国王建立了一个相对集权而有效的战争机器，既击退了东南方好战的土耳其人，也击退了西边饥渴的哈布斯堡家族。然而，马蒂亚斯死后，贵族发动反击，剥夺了他的继任者拉迪斯拉斯维持自己军队的手段。1514年，为再次发动对土耳其人的十字军而做的努力引发了一场大规模的农民起义；对起义的镇压反过来最终把农民彻底贬为奴役状态，并废除了他们更换主人的权利。在农民战争善后过程中接踵而来的权贵争斗中，法学家伊什特万·维尔伯齐写下了贵族对匈牙利习俗的看法，其中包括针对农民的惩罚性法律，以及如下条款：
贵族未经事先法律判决不受逮捕，只服从合法加冕的国王，完全不缴纳任何赋税，并且只有为保卫国家时才可被要求服兵役。最后，反抗权也得到了保障：任何国王若以任何方式侵犯贵族权利，贵族均可反抗。（McNeill 1975 [1964]: 17）

During the later fifteenth century, King Janos Hunyadi and his son, King Matthias Corvinus built a relatively centralized and effective war machine, fighting off both the warlike Turks to their southeast and the hungry Habsburgs to their west. With the death of Matthias, however, the nobility counterattacked, depriving his successor Ladislas of the means to keep his own army. In 1514 the effort to mount yet another crusade against the Turks incited a huge peasant rebellion, whose repression in turn definitively reduced the peasantry to servitude and abolished their right to change masters. In the struggle among magnates that accompanied the settlement of the peasant war, lawyer Istvan Verboczi set down the nobles' view of Hungarian customs, including the retributive laws against the peasantry and the provisions that

nobles enjoyed immunity from arrest without prior legal judgment, were subject only to a legally crowned king, paid no taxes whatsoever, and could be required to render military service only for the defense of the realm. Finally, the right of rebellion was guaranteed against any king who infringed upon the rights of the nobility in any way. (McNeill 1975 [1964]: 17)
维尔伯齐的论著成为匈牙利法律的权威依据，也是“贵族的圣经”（Pamlenyi 1975: 117）。到1526年，匈牙利有了两位经选举产生的国王，而非一位，且两人正彼此交战。难怪在此后半个世纪里，土耳其人能够夺取匈牙利一半的领土！显然，在那个时代，幅员辽阔的国家未必强大。

Verboczi's treatise became the standard authority for Hungarian law and "the bible of the nobility" (Pamlenyi 1975: 117). By 1526, Hungary had not one but two elected kings, and the two were at war with each other. Small wonder that in the following half-century Turks were able to capture half the territory of Hungary! In that era, clearly, large states were not necessarily strong states.
到1490年，穆斯林正从他们在伊比利亚的最后一个据点格拉纳达撤退，但同时在东地中海周围建立一个规模可观的帝国，并向巴尔干渗透。能够派出庞大军队、并对相当大的领土行使某种司法和财政控制的国家，开始出现在欧洲的边缘；城邦也前所未有地武装起来准备陆战。1490年的欧洲地图把大片区域划给英格兰、瑞典、波兰、俄罗斯和奥斯曼帝国，但也标出了数十个公爵领、公国、大主教区、城邦和其他微型国家。

By 1490 Muslims were retreating from their last Iberian outpost, Granada, but building a substantial empire around the eastern Mediterranean and making inroads to the Balkans. States fielding large armies and extending some judicial and fiscal control over good-sized territories were beginning to appear around Europe's edges, and city-states were arming for land war as never before. The European map of 1490 assigns large areas to England, Sweden, Poland, Russia, and the Ottoman Empire, but also marks off dozens of duchies, principalities, archbishoprics, city-states, and other miniature states.

我们能区分出多少个欧洲国家，取决于一些有争议的判断，而这些判断关乎那个时代国家的根本性质：13个瑞士州（截至1513年）和奥斯曼帝国的84个自由市（截至1521年）是否算作独立实体；加泰罗尼亚和格拉纳达这类在名义上自治的阿拉贡和卡斯蒂利亚属地是否应被承认；低地国家这一整块拼图在哈布斯堡霸权下是否构成单一国家（或仅构成一个国家的一部分）；奥斯曼控制下的纳贡国是否各自属于当时的欧洲国家体系。没有任何一套说得通的界定会得出少于80个或多于500个不同单元的结果。我们不妨任意取200作为中位数。当时大约200个形式上自治的欧洲政治实体，平均各控制9,500平方英里，大致相当于今天的萨尔瓦多、莱索托和卡塔尔。

How many European states we distinguish depends on contestable decisions bearing on the very nature of the era's states: whether the 13 Swiss cantons (as of 1513) and the 84 free cities of the Ottoman Empire (as of 1521) count as separate entities, whether such technically autonomous dependencies of Aragon and Castile as Catalonia and Granada deserve recognition, whether the entire patchwork of the Low Countries constituted a single state (or only part of a state) under Habsburg hegemony, whether the tributary states under Ottoman control belonged individually to the European state system of the time. No plausible set of definitions yields fewer than 80 distinct units or more than 500. We might arbitrarily take 200 as the median number. The roughly 200 formally autonomous European political entities of the time controlled an average of 9,500 square miles, roughly the size of today's El Salvador, Lesotho, and Qatar.
1490年欧洲约6200万人口，平均每个国家约310,000人。当然，平均数掩盖了巨大的差异：欧洲数十个较小的国家及其人口可以轻易地塞进俄罗斯辽阔的领土。尽管如此，欧洲正开始整合为以常设军事机构为组织核心、领土彼此分明的国家，军事优势也开始让较大的国家获得更大的生存机会。

Europe's population of approximately 62 million in 1490 divided up into an average of some 310,000 persons per state. Of course, averages obscure enormous variations: scores of Europe's smaller states and their populations would have fitted easily into Russia's vast territory. Nevertheless, Europe was beginning to consolidate into territorially distinct states organized around permanent military establishments, and military superiority was starting to give the larger states better chances of survival.

当然，仅仅是开始。1490年，军队主要由按战役临时雇用的雇佣兵、大领主的扈从和市民民兵组成。在法兰西和勃艮第，常备军已取代了城市民兵，但其他王国鲜有此举。贡赋和私人地租在王室岁入中仍占很大比重。在较大的国家内部，共同体、行会、教会和地方权贵保留了大片豁免与自治的区域。行政主要涉及军事、司法和财政事务。欧洲的中心地带依然充斥着细小的管辖权。由于城邦、城市同盟、王朝帝国、与较大君主国或帝国仅有名义联系的公国，以及条顿骑士团之类的教会实体，都在大陆上（尽管充满争斗地）共存，人们并不清楚我们如今所知的民族国家是否会成为欧洲的主导组织。直到19世纪，随着拿破仑的征服以及随后德意志和意大利的统一，几乎整个欧洲才整合为互不重叠、拥有常设职业武装力量、并对40,000平方英里以上区域内的人口行使实质控制的国家。

Only starting, to be sure. In 1490, armies consisted largely of mercenaries hired by the campaign, clients of great lords, and citizen militias. Standing armies had displaced urban militias in France and Burgundy, but few other realms. Tribute and personal rents still bulked large in royal revenues. Within the larger states, communities, guilds, churches, and regional magnates retained large areas of immunity and self-government. Administration chiefly concerned military, judicial and fiscal affairs. Europe's central zone continued to teem with tiny jurisdictions. Since city-states, leagues of cities, dynastic empires, principalities having only nominal bonds to larger monarchies or empires, and ecclesiastical entities such as the Teutonic Order all coexisted (however contentiously) on the continent, it was not clear that national states as we know them would become Europe's dominant organizations. Not until the nineteenth century, with Napoleon's conquests and the subsequent unifications of Germany and Italy, would almost all of Europe consolidate into mutually exclusive states having permanent, professional armed forces and exercising substantial control over people in areas of 40,000 square miles or more.

在此后四个世纪里，许多战争善后安排和少数刻意建立的联邦大幅减少了欧洲国家的数量。到19世纪，数量趋于稳定。例如1848年初，欧洲有20到100个国家，这取决于如何计算德意志邦联的35个成员、17个教宗国、瑞士22个名义上自治的部分，以及卢森堡和挪威等少数依附性但形式上独立的单位：在那本收录贵族与政治家的名录《哥达年鉴》中，按字母顺序排列的完整名单先从小小的安哈尔特-贝恩堡、安哈尔特-德绍和安哈尔特-科滕开始，然后才轮到规模更大的奥地利、巴登和巴伐利亚。

Over the next four centuries, many war settlements and a few deliberate federations drastically reduced the number of European states. During the nineteenth century, the number stabilized. At the beginning of 1848, for instance, Europe hosted from 20 to 100 states, depending on how one counts the 35 members of the German Confederation, the 17 papal states, the 22 technically autonomous segments of Switzerland, and a few dependent but formally distinct units such as Luxembourg and Norway: in the Almanach de Gotha, that directory of nobles and statesmen, the full alphabetical list then began with tiny Anhalt-Bernburg, Anhalt-Dessau and Anhalt-Kothan before getting to more substantial Austria, Baden, and Bavaria.

德意志帝国和意大利王国的形成带来了重大的整合。到1890年初，国家名录已减至约30个，其中9个是德意志帝国的成员。1918年底，计数约为25个独立国家。尽管随着第一次和第二次世界大战的解决方案，边界发生了重大变化，但20世纪欧洲国家的数量和规模并未发生剧烈变化。如果按照斯莫尔和辛格的做法，只计算那些大到足以产生独立军事影响的国家，我们实际上会发现长期趋势略有逆转：拿破仑战争结束时为21个角逐者，1848年为26个，1980年为29个（此时包括马耳他、塞浦路斯和冰岛）（Small and Singer 1982: 47-50）。

Major consolidations occurred with the formation of the German Empire and the kingdom of Italy. By the start of 1890, the roster of states had declined to about 30, of which nine were members of the German Empire. At the end of 1918, the count stood at around 25 separate states. Although boundaries changed significantly with the settlements of World Wars I and II, the number and size of European states did not change dramatically during the twentieth century. If, following Small and Singer, we count only those states large enough to make an independent military difference, we actually detect a slight reversal of the long-term trend: 21 contenders at the end of the Napoleonic Wars, 26 in 1848, 29 (now including Malta, Cyprus, and Iceland) in 1980 (Small and Singer 1982: 47-50).

与1490年的9,500平方英里相比，1890年的30个国家平均控制63,000平方英里，属于今天的尼加拉瓜、叙利亚和突尼斯一类。1890年的平均国家约有770万居民，而不是1490年的310,000人。若把国家想象为圆形，其平均半径从55英里增至142英里。在55英里半径上，由单一城市的统治者对腹地进行直接控制往往可行；而在142英里半径上，没有专门的监视与干预机构，谁也无法统治。此外，尽管安道尔（175平方英里）、列支敦士登（61）、圣马力诺（24）甚至摩纳哥（0.7）这样的微型国家在大整合中幸存下来，规模上的不平等却随时间急剧下降。

In contrast to the 9,500 square miles of 1490, the 30 states of 1890 controlled an average of 63,000 square miles, which put them in the class of today's Nicaragua, Syria, and Tunisia. Instead of the 310,000 inhabitants of 1490, the average state of 1890 had about 7.7 million. Imagined as circles, states rose from an average radius of 55 miles to 142 miles. At a 55-mile radius, direct control of the hinterland by a single city's rulers was often feasible; at 142 miles, no one governed without a specialized apparatus of surveillance and intervention. Although such microstates as Andorra (175 square miles), Liechtenstein (61), San Marino (24) and even Monaco (0.7) survived the great consolidation, furthermore, inequalities of size declined radically over time.
一般而言，欧洲最后整合为规模可观的民族国家的部分，是那条从意大利北部出发、绕过阿尔卑斯山、沿莱茵河而下直至低地国家的城邦带。德意志和意大利的相继建立，把这些繁荣却别扭的小自治市及其腹地纳入了国家控制。仿佛欧洲人发现，在1790年前后以来盛行的条件下，一个可存续的国家需要至少100英里的半径，而难以统治超过250英里半径的范围。

Generally speaking, the last part of Europe to consolidate into substantial national states was the city-state band running from northern Italy, around the Alps, and down the Rhine to the Low Countries. The successive creations of Germany and Italy brought those prosperous but cantankerous little municipalities and their hinterlands under national control. It is as if Europeans discovered that under the conditions prevailing since 1790 or so, a viable state required a radius of at least 100 miles, and could not easily dominate more than a 250-mile radius.

为了更清楚地看到这一地理格局，我们应当区分城市体系与国家体系。欧洲的城市体系表现的是资本集中之间的变动关系，其国家体系表现的则是强制集中之间的变动关系。欧洲城市形成一个松散的商业与工业等级序列，在这一序列中，任何时点上都有少数城市集群（通常围绕某个单一霸权中心聚合）明显支配其余城市。（当然，欧洲的等级序列只是一个更广阔的城市网络的一部分；该网络在这一时期之初就远远伸入亚洲，并随时间推移扩展到非洲和美洲。）用费尔南·布罗代尔的有用简化来说，从14世纪到20世纪，威尼斯、安特卫普、热那亚、阿姆斯特丹、伦敦和纽约相继位居欧洲城市体系之首。

To see the geographic pattern more clearly, we should distinguish between city systems and systems of states. Europe's systems of cities represented the changing relations among concentrations of capital, its systems of states the changing relations among concentrations of coercion. European cities formed a loose hierarchy of commercial and industrial precedence within which at any point in time a few clusters of cities (usually grouped around a single hegemonic center) clearly dominated the rest. (The European hierarchy, to be sure, formed only part of a vaster urban network that reached far into Asia at the start of the period, and extended to Africa and the Americas as time went on.) In Fernand Braudel's useful simplification, Venice, Antwerp, Genoa, Amsterdam, London, and New York successively topped the European system of cities from the fourteenth century to the twentieth.

就支配地位而言，关键与其说在于规模，不如说在于欧洲贸易、生产和资本积累网络中的中心性。不过，资本集中与城市人口的集中两者吻合得足够紧密，以致占支配地位的城市集群始终也是最大的集群之一。J. C. 拉塞尔运用位序—规模标准，并相当任意地划出边界，勾勒出以佛罗伦萨、巴勒莫、威尼斯、米兰、奥格斯堡、第戎、科隆、布拉格、马格德堡、吕贝克、根特、伦敦、都柏林、巴黎、图卢兹、蒙彼利埃、巴塞罗那、科尔多瓦、托莱多和里斯本为中心的中世纪区域。在从佛罗伦萨到根特的地带，城市更为密集，相应的区域也更小，尤其是在其意大利一端；以各自十个最大城市的总人口衡量，威尼斯（357,000）、米兰（337,000）和佛罗伦萨（296,000）所在区域名列前茅（Russell 1972: 235）。1490年，扬·德·弗里斯对“城市潜力”更精确的计算把大体以安特卫普、米兰和那不勒斯为中心的区域挑出为欧洲城市体系的峰顶，而在1790年，围绕伦敦的那一个地带（包括英吉利海峡对岸的地区）明显占据主导（de Vries 1984: 160-4）。

For dominance, the crucial matter was not so much size as centrality in the European network of trade, production, and capital accumulation. Nevertheless, the concentrations of capital and urban population corresponded closely enough for the dominant
cluster

of cities to be always also one of the largest. Using a rank-size criterion and some rather arbitrary blocking out of boundaries, J. C. Russell delineates medieval regions centering on Florence, Palermo, Venice, Milan, Augsburg, Dijon, Cologne, Prague, Magdeburg, Lubeck, Ghent, London, Dublin, Paris, Toulouse, Montpellier, Barcelona, Cordoba, Toledo, and Lisbon. The cities were denser and the regions correspondingly smaller in the band from Florence to Ghent, especially at its Italian end; as gauged by the total population of their ten largest cities, the regions of Venice (357,000), Milan (337,000), and Florence (296,000) led the pack (Russell 1972: 235). In 1490, Jan de Vries' more precise computation of "urban potential" singles out regions centering approximately on Antwerp, Milan, and Naples as the peaks of the European urban system, while in 1790 the one zone around London (including areas across the English Channel) clearly predominated (de Vries 1984: 160-4).

城市体系与国家体系在欧洲版图上的分布极不均衡，且方式彼此相反。公元990年，阿尔卑斯山以北几乎处处城市既小又稀疏。然而，在一条从博洛尼亚和比萨向北越过阿尔卑斯山、延伸至根特、布鲁日和伦敦的地带，城市更为密集，彼此关系也更为密切。西班牙南部和意大利南部出现了次一级的城市集中区。地中海沿岸各地拥有的城市明显多于大西洋或波罗的海沿岸。当时欧洲最大的两座城市是君士坦丁堡和科尔多瓦，它们不仅是重要的贸易中心，还分别是拜占庭帝国和伍麦叶哈里发国的都城；两城人口都接近五十万（Chandler and Fox 1974: 11）。在此后一千年中，中部地带始终是欧洲城市化程度最高的区域，但它变宽了，其重心也向北移向大西洋各大港口。从1300年起，阿尔卑斯山以北相互连接的城市地带增长得不成比例。

City system and state system spread very unevenly, and in contrasting ways, across the European map. In the year 990, cities were small and scattered almost everywhere north of the Alps. They were nevertheless denser, and relations among them more intense, in a band extending north from Bologna and Pisa across the Alps to Ghent, Bruges, and London. Secondary zones of urban concentration appeared in southern Spain and southern Italy. The Mediterranean lands hosted significantly more cities than those bordering the Atlantic or the Baltic. Europe's two largest cities were then Constantinople and Cordoba, not only major centers of trade but seats respectively of the Byzantine Empire and the Umayyad caliphate; each had a population approaching half a million (Chandler and Fox 1974: 11). Over the next millennium the central band remained Europe's most intensely urban zone, but it widened, and its center of gravity shifted northward toward the great Atlantic ports. From 1300 onward, the band of connected cities north of the Alps grew disproportionately.

城市集群的有无对区域社会生活产生了深刻影响，并显著塑造了国家形成的可能性。在19世纪之前欧洲盛行的生产与运输条件下，规模可观的城市刺激了向乡间延伸许多英里的供给腹地的经济作物种植。商业性农业反过来通常促进了商人、大农户和小地主的繁荣，同时削弱了大土地占有者支配其农村周边人口的能力。（然而，在城市统治阶级同时在腹地拥有大片土地的地方存在一个重要的例外——这在意大利城邦中常常如此；在那里，农民充分感受到了领主控制的全部重量。）

The presence or absence of urban clusters made a profound difference to regional social life, and significantly shaped the possibilities for state formation. Under the conditions of production and transportation prevailing in Europe before the nineteenth century, substantial cities stimulated cash-crop agriculture in tributary areas reaching many miles into the countryside. Commercial agriculture, in its turn, generally promoted the prosperity of merchants, larger peasants, and smaller landlords while reducing the ability of great landholders to dominate the people in their rural surroundings. (A significant exception occurred, however, where the city's ruling class also held extensive land in the hinterland, as was frequently the case in Italian city-states; there the peasantry felt the full weight of lordly control.)

此外，城市深刻影响了周边地区的人口状况。直到不久前，多数欧洲城市都经历自然减少：死亡率超过出生率。因此，即便是停滞的城市也会从附近的市镇和村庄吸引大量移民，而成长中的城市则产生庞大的移民流。这些移民流远大于城市出生缺口加上城市增长率之和，因为一切移民体系都包含大量往返流动；小贩、商人、仆役和工匠常常逐年或逐季地在城乡之间往返摆动。从乡村到城市的净流动通常女性多于男性，结果是性别比（每100名女性对应的男性数）在乡村典型地偏高，在城市则偏低。这样，城市便把自己的印记烙在了周边村民的婚姻机会本身上。

In addition, cities deeply affected the demography of surrounding regions. Until recently, most European cities experienced natural decrease: their death rates exceeded their birth rates. As a result, even stagnant cities drew considerable numbers of migrants from nearby towns and villages, while growing cities generated large migrant streams. The streams were much larger than the urban deficit of births plus the urban rate of growth, since all migration systems involved a great deal of movement back and forth; peddlers, merchants, servants, and artisans frequently oscillated between city and country from year to year or season to season. The net flow from country to city usually included more women than men, with the result that sex ratios (males per 100 females) ran characteristically high in the countryside and low in the city. Thus the city imprinted itself on the very opportunities for marriage of villagers in its surroundings.
城市的商业与人口影响对国家形成产生了显著作用。让我们暂时搁置城市统治阶级和以城市为基地的资本家作为国家权力扩张努力的支持者或反对者的重要性；后文会给他们足够的关注。密集的城乡贸易的存在，为统治者通过关税和消费税征收岁入提供了机会，而相对商业化的经济则使君主在把王权扩展到市镇和村庄时更容易绕过大领主。

The commercial and demographic impact of cities made a significant difference to state formation. Let us leave aside momentarily the importance of urban ruling classes and city-based capitalists as supporters or opponents of efforts to expand state power; they will get plenty of attention later on. The existence of intensive rural-urban trade provided an opportunity for rulers to collect revenues through customs and excise taxes, while the relatively commercialized economy made it easier for monarchs to bypass great landlords as they extended royal power to towns and villages.
此外，城乡关系影响潜在的兵源：士兵将是农村权贵的农奴和佃户，还是来自高流动性和低结婚率地区的雇佣兵、城市民兵，抑或是被征兵队抓走的无地工人？征税机会、地主的权力和兵员的供给深刻影响了国家如何成形。大型城市集群通过粮食供应、移民、贸易、交通和就业机会，把印记烙在周边地区的社会生活上，从而影响了那些试图把国家权力扩展到这些地区的统治者的策略。城市增长的时期只是进一步强化了这些效应。

Relations between city and country, furthermore, affected the potential supply of soldiers: would they be the serfs and tenants of rural magnates, mercenaries from regions of high mobility and low nuptiality, urban militias, or landless workers swept up by pressing squads? Opportunities for taxation, the power of landlords, and the supply of troops deeply affected how states took shape. Through food supply, migration, trade, communications, and opportunities for employment, large urban clusters stamped their mark on the social life in surrounding regions, and thereby influenced the strategies of rulers who attempted to extend state power into those regions. Periods of urban growth only accentuated these effects.

冒着一定风险，并且极大地忽视地区差异，我们可以把公元1000年以来的欧洲城市增长划分为五个阶段：到约1350年为止的一个显著扩张期；1350年至1500年间的一个萧条期，随后是无趋势的起伏；16世纪的加速；17世纪的放缓；最后是1750年之后的巨大加速（Hohenberg and Lees 1985: 7-9）。14世纪毁灭性的瘟疫传播标志着从第一阶段向第二阶段的过渡，伊比利亚人航行到美洲标志着第三阶段的开始，1600年后家庭手工业的增长启动了第四阶段；资本、制造业、服务业和贸易迅速向城市集中则是从第四阶段向第五阶段的转变。

With some risk, and great disregard of regional variation, we can divide European urban growth since 1000 into five phases: a period of considerable expansion to about 1350; a time of depression and then of trendless fluctuation between 1350 and 1500; a sixteenth-century acceleration; a seventeenth-century slowdown, and finally an enormous acceleration after 1750 (Hohenberg and Lees 1985: 7-9). The devastating fourteenth-century spread of plague marks the transition from the first phase to the second, Iberian navigation to America the start of the third phase, the growth of cottage industry after 1600 the launching of the fourth; the implosion of capital, manufacturing, services, and trade into cities the movement from the fourth to the fifth.

从16世纪到18世纪，包括米兰、里昂和曼彻斯特腹地在内的许多欧洲地区经历了原工业化：小型生产单位（包括家户）成倍增加，把它们与远方市场连接起来的小商人也成倍增加。在那场大规模的工业扩张中，是资本流向劳动，而不是相反；农村劳动力无产阶级化了，即决定性地转向为工资而劳动、使用资本家所有的生产资料，但仍留在家庭和小作坊中。于是资本大规模积累，却没有大规模集中。19世纪和20世纪出现了一个相反的运动：资本迅速集中起来，制造业和工人迁往城市，广大乡村地区去工业化。制造商越来越多地把厂址设在能使获取原料和通往商品市场的成本最小化的地方，并正确地假定工人会前来，而费用由厂方以外的人承担。最后一波集中大大加速了欧洲城市化，造就了我们今天所知的这个城市化的大陆。

From the sixteenth to eighteenth centuries, many European regions, including the hinterlands of Milan, Lyon, and Manchester, experienced protoindustrialization: the multiplication of small manufacturing units, including households, and of small merchants who linked them with distant markets. During that great industrial expansion, capital went to labor rather than vice versa; rural labor proletarianized, in the sense of shifting decisively toward work for wages using means of production owned by capitalists, but remained in households and small shops. Capital then accumulated grandly, but did not concentrate enormously. During the nineteenth and twentieth centuries an inverse movement occurred: capital imploded, manufacturing and workers moved to cities, and vast areas of the countryside deindustrialized. Increasingly, manufacturers located where they could minimize the costs of getting to their raw materials and to the markets for their goods, assuming correctly that workers would come to them at someone else's expense. The last burst of concentration greatly accelerated European urbanization, and produced the citified continent we know today.

城市随欧洲总人口一同增长，因此即便城市人口所占份额不变，城镇聚落的数目也会成倍增加；根据现有证据，我们根本不知道1350年之前欧洲人口是否真的变得更城市化。无论如何，居住在城市的比例直到19世纪才急剧上升。根据现有最佳估计，居住在万人以上地点的比例在990年约为5%，1490年为6%，1790年为10%，1890年为30%，而今天接近60%（Bairoch 1985: 182, 282; de Vries 1984: 29-48）。

Cities grew with the European population as a whole, and the number of urban places therefore multiplied even when the urban share of the population was constant; on present evidence, we simply do not know whether the European population actually became more urban before 1350. In any case, the proportion living in cities did not rise dramatically until the nineteenth century. According to the best available estimates, the share in places of 10,000 people or more ran at around 5 percent in 990, 6 percent in 1490, 10 percent in 1790, and 30 percent in 1890, as compared with nearly 60 percent today (Bairoch 1985: 182, 282; de Vries 1984: 29-48).
城市化的时间表反映了欧洲资本的历史。几个世纪里，欧洲流动资本的大部分掌握在散布于大陆各地的小商人手中，他们要么买卖别处生产的货物，要么指导村庄、市镇和小城市中形式上独立的生产者进行制造。像热那亚、奥格斯堡和安特卫普的大资本家那样的人物，在把欧洲彼此连接起来并同世界其余部分连接起来方面发挥了关键作用，但在所有流动中的资本里只占很小的份额。

The timetable of urbanization reflected the history of European capital. For centuries, the bulk of Europe's liquid capital lay in the hands of small merchants who worked scattered through the continent, either trading goods produced elsewhere or guiding manufacturing by formally independent producers in villages, towns, and small cities. Great capitalists like those of Genoa, Augsburg and Antwerp played a crucial part in linking Europe together and with the rest of the world, but held only a small share of all the capital that was in motion.

在1490年之前，零散的证据使人难以作出更详细的定量陈述。不过，保罗·贝罗什的估计和扬·德·弗里斯最近编纂的关于1500年以来欧洲城市化的证据，仍然使一些简单而有说服力的计算成为可能。表2.1显示了1490年之前微不足道的长期城市增长率、16世纪的加速、17世纪的放缓以及1790年之后格外迅速的城市化。到1980年，10,000人这一门槛已失去意义（因此表中出现推测性数字），而足有390座城市拥有100,000或更多居民。事实上，1980年的统计把34.6%的人口定位于至少100,000人的城市。城市增长的巨大加速在1790年之后到来，伴随着19世纪的资本集中、工作场所规模的扩大和大规模运输体系的建立。但在1490年之后的绝大部分时期里，多数城市所能获得的专属腹地在不断缩小。

Before 1490, the scattered evidence makes it difficult to offer any more detailed quantitative statements. Paul Bairoch's estimates and Jan de Vries's recent compilation of evidence concerning European urbanization since 1500 nevertheless make possible some simple but telling computations. Table 2.1 shows the trivial long-run rate of urban growth before 1490, the acceleration of the sixteenth century, the slowdown of the seventeenth, and the exceptional urbanization after 1790. By 1980, the barrier of 10,000 had lost its meaning (hence the speculative numbers in the table), and a full 390 cities had 100,000 inhabitants or more. In fact, the 1980 statistics locate 34.6 percent of the population in cities of at least 100,000. The great acceleration of urban growth arrived after 1790, with the nineteenth-century concentration of capital, increase in scale of workplaces, and creation of mass transport. But through most of the period after 1490, the exclusive hinterlands available to most cities were shrinking in size.

children: 城市与国家趋势的分离改变了一些关键比率。公元990年，欧洲有数以千计类似国家的单元，很可能每二三十个“国家”才有一座万人城市。1490年，每一两个国家就有一座这样的城市。1890年，那个虚构的平均国家拥有约六十座万人以上的城市。仅此一项变化就意味着统治者与被统治者关系的根本改变：控制技术的改变、财政策略的改变、服务需求的改变、政治的改变。

The diverging trends of cities and states changed some critical ratios. In AD 990, with thousands of statelike units, Europe may well have had only one city of 10,000 for every twenty or thirty "states." In 1490, one such city existed for every one or two states. In 1890, the mythical average state had about sixty cities of 10,000 or more. That change alone implied fundamental alterations in the relations between rulers and ruled: altered techniques of control, altered fiscal strategies, altered demands for services, altered politics.
城市塑造国家的命运，主要靠充当资本的容器和分配点。借助资本，城市统治阶级把影响力扩展到城市腹地，并越过广阔的贸易网络。但各城市寡头控制的资本数量各不相同；17世纪的阿姆斯特丹使一度辉煌的布鲁日显得微不足道。此外，城市是资本积累的场所这一事实，使其政治权威能够获得资本、信贷以及对腹地的控制，而这些若被夺取或收编，也可以服务于君主的目的。亚当·斯密有力地陈述了这一核心事实：

Cities shape the destinies of states chiefly by serving as containers and distribution points for capital. By means of capital, urban ruling classes extend their influence through the urban hinterland and across far-flung trading networks. But cities vary in how much capital their oligarchies control; seventeenth-century Amsterdam made once-glorious Bruges look puny. The fact that cities are loci of capital accumulation, furthermore, gives their political authorities access to capital, credit, and control over hinterlands that, if seized or co-opted, can serve the ends of monarchs as well. Adam Smith stated the central fact forcefully:
一个商人和制造商众多的国家……必然拥有这样一批人：他们任何时候都有能力——只要他们愿意——向政府垫付一笔巨款。（Smith 1910 [1778]: II, 392）

A country abounding with merchants and manufacturers ... necessarily abounds with a set of people who have it at all times in their power to advance, if they choose to do so, a very large sum of money to government. (Smith 1910 [1778]: II, 392)
“只要他们愿意”：这一限定语背后隐藏着资本家与国王之间数百年的争斗。然而，亚当·斯密强调在资本充裕地区运作的国家所具有的财政优势，是完全正确的。
If
they choose to do so:

behind that qualifier hide centuries of contention between capitalists and kings. Yet Adam Smith was absolutely right to stress the financial advantages of states that operated in regions of abundant capital.
国家本身主要作为强制手段（尤其是武装力量）的容器和部署者而运作。如今，福利国家、规制国家、把大量精力用于干预经济事务的国家的发展，缓和并遮蔽了强制的中心地位。然而，在我们所考察的这一千年欧洲历史中，军费通常消耗国家预算的大部分，武装力量一般构成政府中最大的单一部门。

States themselves operate chiefly as containers and deployers of coercive means, especially armed force. Nowadays the development of welfare states, of regulatory states, of states that spend a great deal of their effort intervening in economic affairs, has mitigated and obscured the centrality of coercion. Over the millennium of European history we are surveying, however, military expenditure has usually consumed the majority of state budgets, and armed forces have typically constituted the largest single branch of government.

欧洲国家形成的地理格局与城市建设的地理格局之间的差异，对任何意欲掌握统治权的人都构成了尖锐的问题。借用保罗·霍恩伯格和林恩·利斯的概念，我们可以大致区分作为中心地的城市和作为城市网络中节点的城市；所有城市都同属这两个体系，但这两套关系的相对重要性因城而异、差异极大（Hohenberg and Lees 1985: chapter 2）。等级化的中心地体系中介着粮食和衣物等普通货物在连片区域内各聚落之间的流动；原料和粗制货物倾向于沿中心地等级向上流向服务于更广阔市场的较大聚落，而精细和专门化的货物——尤其是那些在该区域体系之外生产的货物——则倾向于从较大地方向下流向较小地方。在我们所考察的这段历史的大部分时间里，初级生产者、地方商人、小贩和定期集市把所售货物的大部分送到消费者手中。

Differences between the geographies of European state formation and city-building presented an acute problem for any would-be ruler. Borrowing from Paul Hohenberg and Lynn Lees, we can make a rough distinction between cities as
central places
and as points in
urban networks;

all cities belong to both systems, but the relative importance of the two sets of relations varies dramatically from one city to another (Hohenberg and Lees 1985: chapter 2). The hierarchical central place system mediates the flow of ordinary goods such as food and clothing among the settlements of a contiguous region; raw materials and rough goods tend to move up the hierarchy of central places toward larger settlements that serve more extensive markets, while fine and specialized goods - especially those produced outside the regional system - tend to move downward from larger places to smaller ones. Over much of the history we are examining, primary producers, local merchants, peddlers, and recurrent public markets brought a major part of the goods sold to their consumers.

另一方面，城市网络把分属不同区域体系的较高层级中心连接起来，这些中心有时相隔数千公里。尽管早在1500年之前很久，木材、小麦、盐和葡萄酒就在欧洲长途运输，但城市网络长期专门从事香料和丝绸这类轻便而昂贵货物的交换。掌握大量资本的商人和金融家在欧洲城市网络中举足轻重。几个世纪里，菲利普·柯廷所称的贸易离散群体发挥了关键作用；犹太人、亚美尼亚人或热那亚人这类地理上分散的商人群体，共享语言、宗教、亲属关系以及（有时）地理出身，通过相互提供信贷、市场信息和优惠待遇，降低了国际贸易的不确定性（Curtin 1984）。即便在贸易离散群体没有在远方中心之间建立关键联系的地方，分散的商人也通常通过航行、私人通信、维持当地代理人和与共同熟人的接触，同其同行保持相识关系。

Urban networks, on the other hand, link higher-level centers in separate regional systems, sometimes removed from each other by thousands of kilometers. Although timber, wheat, salt, and wine traveled great distances in Europe well before 1500, urban networks long specialized in the exchange of light, expensive goods such as spices and silks. Merchants and financiers with substantial capital at their disposal figured importantly in Europe's urban networks. For centuries, what Philip Curtin calls trade diasporas had a crucial role; geographically dispersed mercantile groups such as Jews, Armenians, or Genoese, who shared language, religion, kinship, and (sometimes) geographic origin reduced the uncertainties of international trade by extending each other credit, market information, and preferential treatment (Curtin 1984). Even where trade diasporas did not make the crucial links among distant centers, dispersed merchants commonly maintained acquaintance with their colleagues by means of voyages, personal correspondence, maintenance of local representatives, and contact with mutual acquaintances.

一个掌握强制手段的统治者，只要付出一定努力，就能夺取一个或多个中心地等级体系的全部领土，甚至重塑某个等级体系，使之大致与其国家的边界相符；到16世纪，英格兰与伦敦的中心地体系之间、法兰西与巴黎的中心地体系之间，已经出现了大致的对应。但要使一个国家与远距离城市网络的轮廓相吻合，则既罕见又困难。汉萨同盟这样的城市同盟以及威尼斯和葡萄牙这样的海上帝国曾一度接近做到这一点，但总是发现自己要同对其某个贸易据点提出主张的领土统治者竞争或讨价还价；一个横亘于威尼斯最有利可图的商路上的奥斯曼帝国的巩固，使威尼斯人在12世纪和13世纪编织起来的那个壮观商业帝国注定走向覆灭。另一方面，商人致力于远距离贸易的领土国家，总是发现自己面对着强大的经济行动者，这些行动者的对外关系是国家永远无法完全控制的，而且一旦统治者的要求变得难以承受，他们携资本逃往另一处营业地点也相对容易。强制的地理格局与资本的地理格局之间长期存在的不一致，保证了围绕它们组织起来的社会关系将以各自独特的方式演化。

A coercion-wielding ruler can, with a certain amount of effort, capture the entire territory of one or more central-place hierarchies, and even reshape a hierarchy to correspond approximately with the limits of his state; by the sixteenth century, a rough correspondence had emerged between England and the central-place system of London, between France and the central-place system of Paris. But it is rare and difficult to match a state to the contours of a long-distance urban network. Federations such as the Hanseatic League and maritime empires such as those of Venice and Portugal came close for a time, but always found themselves competing or bargaining with territorial rulers who laid claim on one or another of their trading outposts; the consolidation of an Ottoman empire athwart Venice's most lucrative trade routes doomed the spectacular mercantile empire Venetians had stitched together during the twelfth and thirteenth centuries. Territorial states whose merchants devoted themselves to long-distance trade, on the other hand, always found themselves confronted with powerful economic actors whose external relations they could never entirely control, and who found it relatively easy to escape with their capital to another business site if the ruler's demands became unbearable. The long-lasting discrepancy between the geographies of coercion and of capital guaranteed that the social relations organized around them would evolve in distinctive ways.

就整个欧洲而言，公元900年至今国家在控制资本和控制强制两方面的变化，沿着两条平行的弧线展开。起初，在“家产制”时代，欧洲君主一般以贡赋或地租的形式，从直接处于自己控制之下的土地和人口中抽取所需的资本——而且往往受到关于其可索取数额的严格契约限制。在“经纪”时代（尤其是约1400年至1700年间），他们严重依赖形式上独立的资本家提供贷款、管理产生收入的企业和征税。然而到18世纪，“国家化”的时代已经到来；许多君主把财政机构直接并入国家结构，并大幅削减独立承包人的参与。最近一个世纪左右，即“专业化”时代，带来了财政组织与军事组织之间更明显的分离，以及国家对固定资本监管的日益介入。
Over Europe as a whole, alterations in state control of capital and of coercion between AD 900 and the present have followed two parallel arcs. At first, during the age of
patrimonialism,

European monarchs generally extracted what capital they needed as tribute or rent from lands and populations that lay under their immediate control - often within stringent contractual limits on the amounts they could demand. In the time of
brokerage

(especially between 1400 and 1700 or so), they relied heavily on formally independent capitalists for loans, for management of revenue-producing enterprises, and for collection of taxes. By the eighteenth century, however, the time of
nationalization

had come; many sovereigns were incorporating the fiscal apparatus directly into the state structure, and drastically curtailing the involvement of independent contractors. The last century or so, the age of
specialization,
has brought a sharper separation of fiscal from military organization and an increasing involvement of states in the oversight of fixed capital.

在强制方面，也发生了类似的演化。在家产制时期，君主从负有个人服役义务的扈从、封臣和民兵那里获取武装力量——但同样受到重要的契约限制。在经纪时代（同样尤其是1400年至1700年间），他们日益转向由承包人提供给他们的雇佣军，这些承包人保留着相当大的行动自由。接下来，在国家化时期，君主把陆军和海军直接吸收进国家的行政结构，最终不再依赖外国雇佣兵，而是从本国公民中招募或征召大部分兵员。自19世纪中叶起，在一个专业化阶段中，欧洲国家巩固了由庞大文官官僚机构支撑的公民军队体系，并分化出专门在战争之外使用强制的警察力量。

On the side of coercion, a similar evolution took place. During the period of patrimonialism, monarchs drew armed force from retainers, vassals, and militias who owed them personal service - but again within significant contractual limits. In the age of brokerage (again especially between 1400 and 1700) they turned increasingly to mercenary forces supplied to them by contractors who retained considerable freedom of action. Next, during nationalization, sovereigns absorbed armies and navies directly into the state's administrative structure, eventually turning away from foreign mercenaries and hiring or conscripting the bulk of their troops from their own citizenries. Since the mid-nineteenth century, in a phase of specialization, European states have consolidated the system of citizen militaries backed by large civilian bureaucracies, and split off police forces specialized in the use of coercion outside of war.

到19世纪，多数欧洲国家已把武装力量和财政机制内化；它们由此削弱了包税人、军事承包者和其他独立中间人的治理作用。此后，统治者继续与资本家及其他阶级就信贷、岁入、人力和战争必需品讨价还价。而讨价还价又对国家提出了众多新的要求：养老金、对穷人的给付、公共教育、城市规划，等等。在这一过程中，国家从放大的战争机器转变为多重目标的组织。它们控制强制与资本的努力仍在继续，但伴随着各种各样规制性、补偿性、分配性和保护性的活动。

By the nineteenth century, most European states had internalized both armed forces and fiscal mechanisms; they thus reduced the governmental roles of tax farmers, military contractors, and other independent middlemen. Their rulers then continued to bargain with capitalists and other classes for credit, revenues, manpower, and the necessities of war. Bargaining, in its turn, created numerous new claims on the state: pensions, payments to the poor, public education, city planning, and much more. In the process, states changed from magnified war machines into multiple-purpose organizations. Their efforts to control coercion and capital continued, but in the company of a wide variety of regulatory, compensatory, distributive, and protective activities.

在19世纪之前，各国在两大变革进程的相对时序和强度上差异显著。荷兰国家在一个多世纪里租用庞大的陆军和海军，超前地实行了国家对财政的管理，却长期受制于阿姆斯特丹及其他商业城市的资本家。有时，荷兰国家确实消融为其主要市镇政府的集合。另一方面，在卡斯蒂利亚，陆军（往往是在西班牙境外雇用的）占主导地位；那里的君主制通过把商人变成食利者、并依赖殖民地岁入偿付他们，从而取得了商人的信贷。葡萄牙、波兰、意大利各城邦以及神圣罗马帝国的诸国，遵循了这两条弧线的其他组合方式，从而创造了截然不同的国家结构。

Before the nineteenth century, states differed markedly in the relative timing and intensity of the two main processes of change. The Dutch state rented large armies and navies for a century or more, adopted state management of finances precociously, yet long remained beholden to the capitalists of Amsterdam and other commercial cities. At moments, indeed, the Dutch state dissolved into the governments of its major municipalities. In Castile, on the other hand, land forces - often hired outside of Spain - prevailed; there the monarchy captured the credit of merchants by turning them into rentiers and by relying on colonial revenues for their reimbursement. Portugal, Poland, Italian city-states, and the states of the Holy Roman Empire followed other combinations of the two arcs, and thereby created distinctly different state structures.

为什么欧洲国家走上了如此不同的轨迹，却又几乎都朝着在资本和强制方面更加集中的方向前进？两个秘密解释了其中大部分的复杂性。第一个是规模不等、不断变动的国家之间围绕贸易和领土进行的持续而激烈的竞争，这使战争成为欧洲历史的驱动力。第二个在于加布里埃尔·阿尔当所称的国家的“生理机制”：即国家获取并分配用以开展其主要活动的手段的那些过程。在与此相关的历史的大部分时间里，关键手段尤其是强制手段，即战争手段。强制手段显然在战争制造（攻击外部对手）、国家制造（攻击内部对手）和保护（攻击依附于国家者的敌人）中发挥了作用。强制手段也在国家行使抽取（从臣民人口中抽取国家活动的手段）和裁决（解决该人口成员之间的争端）时发挥作用。只有在涉及生产和分配时，强制手段才不是国家活动的主要支撑——即便在那里，强制的程度也因国而异。例如，在国家对盐、武器或烟草产品的生产建立自己的垄断的地方，它们通常是以武力做到这一点的；当统治者决定垄断相关商品的分配时，走私品通常就成了走私品。

Why did European states follow such different trajectories, yet almost all head in the direction of greater concentration with respect to capital and coercion? Two secrets account for most of the complexity. The first is the continuous, aggressive competition for trade and territory among changing states of unequal size, which made war a driving force in European history. The second lies in what Gabriel Ardant called the "physiology" of states: the processes by which they acquire and allocate the means of carrying on their major activities. For most of the history that concerns us here, the crucial means were especially coercive, the means of war. Coercive means obviously played a part in warmaking (attacking external rivals), statemaking (attacking internal rivals), and protection (attacking the enemies of the state's clients). Coercive means also came into play in a state's exercise of extraction (drawing the means of state activity from its subject population) and adjudication (settling disputes among members of that population). Only when it came to production and distribution were coercive means not major supports of the state's activity - and even there the degree of coercion varied from state to state. Where states established their own monopolies over the production of salt, arms, or tobacco products, for example, they typically did so by force of arms; contraband usually becomes contraband when rulers decide to monopolize the distribution of the commodity in question.

强制手段把武器与懂得使用武器的人结合在一起。（我确实是指男人；在西方经验中，女性在强制组织的建构和使用中所起的作用小得惊人，这一事实无疑有助于解释她们在国家中的从属地位。）国家的代理人要集中强制手段并阻止他人这样做，在下列程度上会更容易：（a）武器生产涉及秘传知识、稀有材料或大量资本；（b）很少有群体具备独立动员大量人力的能力；（c）很少有人知道把武器与人结合起来的诀窍。长期来看，欧洲国家的统治者利用了所有这些条件，朝着垄断其领土内较大规模的强制手段集中——军队、警察力量、武器、监狱和法庭——的方向推进。

Coercive means combine weapons with men who know how to use them. (I do mean men; in Western experience, women have played an amazingly small part in the construction and use of coercive organization, a fact that surely helps account for their subordinate position within states.) Agents of states have an easier time concentrating coercion, and keeping others from doing so, to the extent that (a) production of weapons involves esoteric knowledge, rare materials, or substantial capital, (b) few groups have the independent capacity to mobilize large numbers of men and (c) few people know the secrets of combining weapons with men. Over the long run, the rulers of European states took advantage of all these conditions to move toward monopolies of the larger concentrations of coercive means within their territories: armies, police forces, weapons, prisons, and courts.

国家以多种不同方式使用集中的强制。在公元990年之后的头几个世纪里，国王直接控制的武装力量很少比其主要追随者多多少。供养和维持武装人员的后勤使建立常备军昂贵得难以承受。王室军队通常由国王的小规模常备部队，加上由追随者召唤、只是暂时离开平民生活的部队组成。国王的在场强化了战士之间的个人联系：“一条普遍规则是，国王应亲自指挥每一场重要战役。年龄无关紧要；奥托三世率军征讨萨克森人时（991年）只有11岁，亨利四世1063年对匈牙利人开战时只有13岁”（Contamine 1984: 39）。行进中的王室军队主要靠征用（理论上应由王室国库偿还）和劫掠（则不予偿还）为生；当然，这一区别在几个世纪里始终模糊不清。

States used concentrated coercion in a number of different ways. During the first few centuries after AD 990, kings rarely had much more armed force under their direct control than did their chief followers. The logistics of feeding and maintaining armed men made the establishment of standing armies prohibitively expensive. A royal army normally consisted of the king's small permanent force plus troops who came only temporarily from civilian life at his followers' call. The king's presence reinforced the personal connections among warriors: "It was a general rule that the king should command in person every important campaign. Age did not matter; Otto III was 11 when he led his army against the Saxons (991) and Henry IV 13 when he went to war against the Hungarians in 1063'' (Contamine 1984: 39). Royal armies on the move lived largely from requisition (which was theoretically to be repaid from the royal treasury) and plunder (which was not); the distinction, to be sure, remained unclear for centuries.

城市通常组织市民民兵，他们守卫城墙、巡逻街道、介入公共冲突，并不时与城市或王国的敌人作战。西班牙的市政民兵是个例外；他们在基督教国王征服穆斯林伊比利亚的过程中发挥了核心作用，这一事实反映在收复失地运动之后授予贵族主导的市镇的巨大权力之中，也反映在 caballero（骑马者）与 péon（步兵）之间的区分结晶为一种持久而普遍的社会分野之中（Powers 1988）。在其他地方，国王一般都设法限制市民可以支配的独立武装力量，理由非常充分：市民很可能为自己的利益使用武力，包括抵抗王室的要求。

Cities commonly organized citizen militias which guarded walls, patrolled streets, intervened in public conflicts, and now and then fought battles against enemies of city or of the kingdom. Spanish municipal militias were exceptional; they played the central part in the conquest of Muslim Iberia by Christian kings, a fact reflected in the great powers vested in the noble-dominated municipalities after the Reconquista, and in the crystallization of the distinction between
caballero
(horseman) and
péon

(foot soldier) into an enduring and general social division (Powers 1988). Elsewhere, kings generally sought to limit the independent armed force at the disposition of townsmen, for the very good reason that townsmen were quite likely to use force in their own interest, including resistance to royal demands.
这些形形色色的军事力量面对着许多不在王室直接控制下行动的武装群体：其中包括尚未被动员为王室服役的某些领主的扈从、盗匪（往往是复员的士兵，未经王室许可继续劫掠）和海盗（常常在王室或城市的保护下活动）。强制手段的积聚规模不大，却分布极广；集中程度很低。即便如此，统治者在集中强制方面所做的仍比任何其他人都多。

These various military forces confronted many groups of armed men who did not operate under direct royal control: among others, the retainers of particular lords who were not currently mobilized for royal service, bandits (who were often demobilized soldiers, continuing their plunder without royal assent), and pirates (who frequently worked with royal or civic protection). Accumulations of coercive means were modest but very widely spread; concentration was slight. Even so, rulers were doing more to concentrate coercion than was anyone else.
最终，国家开始运作多支武装力量，它们全都官僚化了，并或多或少地整合进国家行政之中。就连以反复把国家权力下放给代理人和显贵而闻名的西班牙，也一再努力使其武装力量脱离其平民环境。例如，腓力二世有意把武装力量置于政府的直接控制之下；在其父查理五世统治时期，这些武装力量的指挥权几乎成了显贵的私人财产。
到1580年，整个军事机构已归还王室，由王室大臣管理；西班牙、那不勒斯和西西里的桨帆船队在1574—6年短暂而不成功地恢复承包制之后，重新回到 administración（行政管理）之下；地中海舰队和北非驻军的补给由塞维利亚的王室军需部门控制；武器工业和硝石制造者处于严格的王室监督之下，火药制造则是王室垄断。（Thompson 1976: 6-7）

Eventually states came to operate multiple armed forces, all of them bureaucratized and more or less integrated into the national administration. Even Spain, notorious for the repeated devolution of state powers to its agents and grandees, made repeated efforts to detach its armed forces from their civilian surroundings. Philip II, for example, deliberately placed under direct government control armed forces whose commands had almost been private possessions of grandees during the reign of his father, Charles V.

By 1580, the entire military establishment had been restored to the Crown and was being run by royal ministers; the galleys of Spain, Naples and Sicily, after a brief and unsuccessful return to contracting in 1574-6, were back in
administración,

the provisioning of the Mediterranean fleets and the garrisons of north Africa was controlled by the royal commissariat in Seville, the arms industries and the saltpetre makers were under strict royal supervision, and the manufacture of gunpowder was a royal monopoly. (Thompson 1976: 6-7)
在此后半个世纪里，财政和行政上的紧迫需要使西班牙重新回到广泛的承包和地方控制；尽管如此，武装力量从此以后仍作为民族国家中彼此有别的分化部门运作。事实上，到19世纪，西班牙军队的组织独立性和自主性已如此之强，以致能作为一个独立的力量反复干预国家政治（Ballbe 1983）。

During the next half-century the exigencies of financing and administration led Spain back to extensive contracting and local control; nevertheless, the armed forces henceforth operated as distinct, differentiated branches of the national state. Indeed by the nineteenth century the Spanish army acquired such distinctness and autonomy as to intervene repeatedly as a separate force in national politics (Ballbé 1983).
在西班牙和其他地方，陆军与海军之间泾渭分明的分工很早就出现，并延续下来。就全国范围而言，陆军（一般专门对付其他武装力量）与警察力量（一般专门控制未武装或轻武装的个人和小群体）之间的分工，直到相当晚近才变得普遍——在多数国家是在19世纪。到那时，强制力的积聚规模巨大、高度集中，因而极不平等。到19世纪，各国已成功地把自己武装得令人印象深刻，并几乎解除了平民人口的武装。

In Spain and elsewhere, a sharp division between armies and navies emerged early, and endured. At a national scale, the division between armies (generally specialized in combatting other armed forces) and police forces (generally specialized in the control of unarmed or lightly-armed individuals and small groups) only became general quite late -in most countries, during the nineteenth century. By that time accumulations of coercive force were large, concentrated, and therefore very unequal. By the nineteenth century, states had succeeded in arming themselves impressively, and in almost disarming their civilian populations.
图2.6把城市与国家的关系图式化为资本与强制的互动。在对角线之上，强制超过资本；在其之下，资本超过强制。这一区分适用于单个城市；阿姆斯特丹和巴塞罗那这样的欧洲港口通常资本极为充裕，强制机构却相对薄弱；另一方面，柏林和马德里这样的君主驻地，在强制方面的位置远高于在资本方面的位置。

Figure 2.6 schematizes the relationship between cities and states as an interaction of capital and coercion. Above the diagonal, coercion outran capital; below it, capital outstripped coercion. The distinction applies to individual cities; European ports such as Amsterdam and Barcelona typically wallowed in capital while having relatively thin coercive apparatuses; seats of monarchs such as Berlin and Madrid, on the other hand, stood much higher with respect to coercion than to capital.

children: 这一区分也适用于国家的环境。这一千年中欧洲变化的总方向无疑是沿对角线向上，朝向资本与强制两者越来越高的集中。但不同的国家在同一总方向上遵循了不同的路径。勃兰登堡—普鲁士成长于强制充裕、资本匮乏的环境中，即便当它把控制扩展到资本集中的莱茵兰城市时，仍带着其早期环境的印记。丹麦通常能支配比斯堪的纳维亚其余部分更多的资本，而在国家努力中投入军事力量建设较少。

The distinction also applies to the environments of states. The general direction of European change over the millennium undoubtedly ran up the diagonal, toward greater and greater concentrations of both capital and coercion. But different states followed different paths in the same general direction. Brandenburg-Prussia grew up in a coercion-rich, capital-poor environment, and bore the marks of its early environment even when it extended its control to the capitalist cities of the Rhineland. Denmark usually had greater concentrations of capital at its disposal than the rest of Scandinavia, and invested less of its state effort in the building up of military might.

条顿骑士团（耶路撒冷圣玛丽医院修会）走过一条不规则的路径：从12世纪末在圣地从事掠夺性十字军活动（因而深深卷入海洋商业的海盗世界），到13世纪成为特兰西瓦尼亚一大片地区的统治者，再到成为异教普鲁士的征服者和殖民者，约从1300年到16世纪在那里以大领主的风格进行统治。骑士团用大约三十年时间跨越了从资本密集型国家形成到强制密集型国家形成的界线。马耳他骑士团（先后又称耶路撒冷圣约翰医院骑士团和罗得岛骑士团）同样曲折前行，却落脚在一个非常不同的位置：

The Teutonic Knights (the Order of St Mary's Hospital at Jerusalem) took an irregular path: from freebooting crusaders in the Holy Land (hence heavily involved in the piratical world of oceanic commerce) at the end of the twelfth century to governors of a large piece of Transylvania during the thirteenth century to conquerors and colonizers of pagan Prussia, where they ruled in the style of great landlords from about 1300 into the sixteenth century. The Knights crossed the line from capital-intensive to coercion-intensive state formation in about thirty years. The Knights of Malta (also known successively as the Knights Hospitallers of St John of Jerusalem and the Knights of Rhodes) likewise zigged and zagged, but ended up in a very different location:
……一个约在1100年诞生于圣地的修会，几乎立即转变为保卫东方拉丁诸国的军事修会，随后在退往塞浦路斯（1291年）、再退往罗得岛（1309年）的过程中转向海上生涯，最后在1530年作为西西里国王宗主权下的主权国家被安置于马耳他时，被迫专门从事这一海上事业。（Fontenay 1988a: 362）

... a religious order born in the Holy Land toward 1100, but almost immediately transformed into a military order in defense of the East's Latin states, then moving to a maritime career in its retreat to Cyprus (1291) and then Rhodes (1309), and finally forced to devote itself full time to that calling at its installation in Malta as a sovereign state under the suzerainty of the King of Sicily in 1530. (Fontenay 1988a: 362)
骑士团以马耳他为基地，致力于合法化的海盗活动，从而走上了一条比他们在圣地时的邻居更为资本密集的道路。因此，我们可以把这个图示看作一幅地图，标示出不同欧洲国家在其与领土内城市的各种互动中所走的多种路径。

By devoting themselves to legalized piracy from their Maltese base, the Knights followed a more capital-intensive course than their onetime neighbors in the Holy Land. Thus we can think of the diagram as a map of the multiple paths taken by different European states in their various interactions with the cities in their territories.

资本—强制图示体现了我第一章勾勒的论点：任何特定地区最强大的统治者都为所有人设定战争的条件；较小的统治者面临一种选择：要么顺应强大邻国的要求，要么为战争准备付出非同寻常的努力。战争和战争准备使统治者不得不从掌握关键资源——人力、武器、补给，或购买这些东西的钱——并且除非受到强大压力或得到补偿否则不愿交出这些资源的他人那里抽取战争手段。在其他国家的要求与报偿所设定的限度内，围绕战争手段的抽取和斗争创造了国家的核心组织结构。国家领土内主要社会阶级的组织方式及其与国家的关系，显著影响了统治者抽取资源所采用的策略、他们遭遇的抵抗、由此产生的斗争、抽取和斗争所确立的持久组织类型，并因此影响了资源抽取的效率。

The capital-coercion diagram embodies the argument I sketched in the first chapter: the most powerful rulers in any particular region set the terms of war for all; smaller rulers faced a choice between accommodating themselves to the demands of powerful neighbors and putting exceptional efforts into preparations for war. War and preparations for war involved rulers in extracting the means of war from others who held the essential resources - men, arms, supplies, or money to buy them - and who were reluctant to surrender them without strong pressure or compensation. Within limits set by the demands and rewards of other states, extraction and struggle over the means of war created the central organizational structures of states. The organization of major social classes within a state's territory, and their relations to the state, significantly affected the strategies rulers employed to extract resources, the resistance they met, the struggle that resulted, the sorts of durable organization that extraction and struggle laid down, and therefore the efficiency of resource extraction.
主要社会阶级的组织方式及其与国家的关系，在欧洲的强制密集型地区（城市稀少、农业占主导，直接强制在生产中起主要作用的地区）与资本密集型地区（城市众多、商业占主导，市场、交换和市场导向的生产盛行的地区）之间差异显著。主要阶级对国家提出的要求，以及它们对国家的影响力，也相应地不同。因此，不同抽取策略的相对成功，以及统治者实际采用的策略，在强制密集型地区与资本密集型地区之间差别很大。

The organization of major social classes, and their relations to the state varied significantly from Europe's coercion-intensive regions (areas of few cities and agricultural predominance, where direct coercion played a major part in production) to its capital-intensive regions (areas of many cities and commercial predominance, where markets, exchange, and market-oriented production prevailed). The demands major classes made on the state, and their influence over the state, varied correspondingly. The relative success of different extractive strategies, and the strategies rulers actually applied, therefore varied significantly from coercion-intensive to capital-intensive regions.

因此，国家的组织形式在欧洲这些不同地区遵循了明显不同的轨迹。在特定时代和欧洲特定地区，哪一种国家占据主导，差别极大。直到这一千年晚期，民族国家才相对于城邦、帝国和其他欧洲常见国家形式取得明显优势。尽管如此，战争规模的不断扩大，以及欧洲国家体系通过商业、军事和外交互动而日益紧密地联结，最终使那些能够派出庞大常备军的国家获得了战争制造的优势；能够同时利用庞大农村人口、资本家和相对商业化经济的国家胜出。它们设定了战争的条件，其国家形式成为欧洲的主导形式。最终，欧洲各国汇聚于这一形式：民族国家。

As a consequence, the organizational forms of states followed distinctly different trajectories in these different parts of Europe. Which sort of state prevailed in a given era and part of Europe varied greatly. Only late in the millennium did national states exercise clear superiority over city-states, empires, and other common European forms of state. Nevertheless, the increasing scale of war and the knitting together of the European state system through commercial, military, and diplomatic interaction eventually gave the warmaking advantage to those states that could field great standing armies; states having access to a combination of large rural populations, capitalists, and relatively commercialized economies won out. They set the terms of war, and their form of state became the predominant one in Europe. Eventually European states converged on that form: the national state.

在资本—强制图示所标出的每一条路径之内，较早的步伐约束着较晚的步伐。如果城市统治阶级在某个国家最初的整合中发挥了重要作用（如他们在荷兰那样），那么很久之后该国仍以资产阶级制度的形式带着它们的印记。如果一个国家起源于对以农村为主的人口的征服（如历代的俄罗斯帝国那样），它便继续对在其境内成长起来的城市提供很小的空间；在此类地区，随着君主为换取武装地主间歇性的兵役而授予他们财政特权和可观的本地管辖权，庞大的贵族群体成长起来。

Within each path marked out in the capital-coercion diagram, earlier steps constrained later ones. If urban ruling classes played important parts in the initial consolidation of a given state (as they did in Holland), long afterward the state bore their imprint in the form of bourgeois institutions. If a state originated in conquest of largely rural populations (as did successive Russian empires) it continued to offer little scope to such cities as grew up in its midst; in such regions, large nobilities grew up as monarchs granted fiscal privileges and substantial local jurisdictions to arms-bearing landlords in return for their intermittent military service.

在过去这一千年的大部分时间里，欧洲的城市与国家一直在进行一系列“危险的结合”，这是一种爱恨交织的关系：双方对彼此既不可或缺，又难以忍受。城市及其资本家从经营国家的强制专家那里获得其商业和工业活动所不可或缺的保护，但他们有理由担心自己的赚钱活动受到干扰，担心自己的资源被挪用去打仗、备战或支付以往的战争。国家与军人依赖以城市为基地的资本家提供招募和维持武装力量所需的财力，但他们也有理由担心城市、城市的商业利益及其工人阶级所激起的对国家权力的抵抗。城市与国家在以保护换取资本使用权的交换中找到了不安地讨价还价的基础，但直到19世纪，这类交易始终脆弱。
Through most of the last millennium, European cities and states have carried on a series of
liaisons dangereuses,

love-hate affairs in which each became at once indispensable and insufferable to the other. Cities and their capitalists drew indispensable protection for their commercial and industrial activity from the specialists in coercion who ran states, but rightly feared interference in their money-making and diversion of their resources to war, preparation for war, or payment for past wars. States and military men depended on city-based capitalists for the financial means to recruit and sustain armed force, yet properly worried about the resistance to state power engendered by cities, their commercial interests, and their working classes. Cities and states found the grounds for uneasy bargains in the exchange of protection for access to capital, but until the nineteenth century such bargains remained fragile.

如今很难想象17世纪墨西拿的种种谋划，那是西西里最重商的城市。西西里已成为落后的象征，以致我们轻易忘记它作为辉煌王国驻地、地中海粮仓和大国争夺对象的光荣的数百年历史。西西里——先是穆斯林统治，后是诺曼人统治——于1282年落入阿拉贡的统治之下，并随着16世纪统一君主制的形成而成为西班牙的财产。墨西拿的商人寡头在西班牙统治下愤懑不平，因为这种统治为了王朝利益而限制他们进入外国市场，尤其限制他们对西西里丝货出口的控制。1674年，西班牙（与荷兰松散结盟）正与法兰西（当时与英格兰松散结盟）交战。墨西拿的领袖们关闭城门不让西班牙军队进入，向法兰西、英格兰和奥斯曼帝国求援，力争建立一个由外国国王从墨西拿统治的独立西西里，要求其港口免缴关税，并欢迎一位法兰西的西西里总督及其军队。

These days it is hard to imagine the seventeenth-century machinations of Messina, Sicily's most mercantile city. Sicily has become such an emblem for backwardness that we easily forget the many centuries of Sicilian glory as a seat of brilliant kingdoms, a breadbasket for the Mediterranean, and an object of competition among great powers. Sicily - once Muslim, and then Norman - had come under Aragonese rule in 1282, and had become a property of Spain with the sixteenth-century formation of a unified monarchy. The merchant-oligarchs of Messina chafed under Spanish rule, which cramped their access to foreign markets, and especially their control over the export of Sicilian silk, in favor of dynastic interests. In 1674, Spain (loosely allied with Holland) was at war with France (loosely allied, for the moment, with England). Messina's leaders closed their gates to Spanish troops, appealed for help to France, England, and the Ottoman Empire, bid for an independent Sicily ruled from Messina by a foreign king, asked for their port to be free of customs, and welcomed a French governor of Sicily with his troops.

然而三年之后，墨西拿人厌倦了法兰西的占领，而法兰西人也失去了在一个背信弃义的人民中间维持军事机构的热情。当法兰西人撤退、显要家族出逃之后，留下来的商人组成市民卫队，为西班牙统治的回归而欢呼（Mack Smith 1968a: 225-30）。在西西里和其他地方，当外部事件改变了国家的军事地位或城市的商业地位，或者当一方把优势推得过远时，国家与城市的契约便容易破裂。统治者和资本家不断重新谈判它们的相对地位。

After three years, however, the Messinans tired of French occupation as the French lost their enthusiasm for maintaining a military establishment amid a perfidious population. When the French withdrew and the leading families fled, the remaining merchants formed a civic guard and cheered the return of Spanish rule (Mack Smith 1968a: 225-30). In Sicily and elsewhere, state-city compacts broke easily when external events altered the state's military position or the cities' commercial position, and when one side or the other pushed its advantage too far. Rulers and capitalists constantly renegotiated their relative positions.
然而，并非每一对国家—城市都维持同样的关系。远非如此：这一模式在欧洲各地差别极大，并随世纪更迭而急剧变化。威尼斯建立自己的商业帝国，后来才着手征服大陆领土；波兰领主阻碍了其城市的发展；而巴黎尽管屡屡反叛，却很好地服务于法兰西君主制。

Not every state-city pair, however, maintained the same relationship. Far from it: the pattern varied sharply from one part of Europe to another, and changed dramatically over the centuries. Venice created its own commercial empire and only later undertook the conquest of mainland territory, Polish lords stunted the growth of their cities, while Paris, for all its rebellions, served the French monarchy well.

回到资本—强制图示，我们可以像图2.7那样勾勒若干不同欧洲地区的故事。于是，按照该图示，波兰国家生活在强制充裕、资本匮乏的环境中，而且实际上随着大贵族夺取各自的强制和资本份额，它面临着两者集中程度的下降。斯堪的纳维亚各国一般始于可观的强制集中，最终走向对集中资本的更高控制水平。相比之下，德意志小邦、意大利城邦和荷兰共和国在其轨迹的起点上拥有可观的资本集中，但武装力量薄弱而时断时续，只是逐渐走向常设的、集中的军事机构。

Returning to the capital-coercion diagram, we might sketch the stories of a number of different European areas as in figure 2.7. Thus, according to the diagram, the Polish state lived in a coercion-rich, capital-poor environment, and actually faced a decline in the concentrations of both as great nobles seized their shares of coercion and capital. Scandinavian states generally began amid substantial concentrations of coercion, and eventually moved toward higher levels of control over concentrated capital. Small German states, Italian city-states, and the Dutch Republic, in contrast, began their trajectories in the presence of substantial concentrations of capital but weak, intermittent armed force, only gradually moving toward permanent, concentrated military establishments.
